text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli army chief of staff warns that Palestinian anger rising.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, Foreign Minister Levy deny deals over jobs.
- Netanyahu rejects U.S. report on settlements.
HAARETZ
- Infrastructure Minister Sharon proposes extending Israeli sovereignty to Israel's water sources in West Bank.
- Netanyahu, Israeli Ambassador to Washington Ben-Elissar meet; ambassador says they won't replace me.
- Leader of Shas religious party, a key government coalition partner: We trusted the prime minister but now it's time we did our part to save the peace process.
- Absorption minister and member of immigrant party, key coalition member: If the mess in the government continues, the ministers will say they're not willing for more.
- 61 percent gap between wages of men and women in Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Palestinian President Arafat: We will impose death penalty on land agents that sell land to Jews.
- Netanyahu tending toward not replacing Ben-Elissar.
- Israel Lands Fund owns large tract of land in Jordan.
MAARIV
- Night meeting to determine fate of Ben-Elissar.
- Anxiety in Jerusalem over another cut in U.S. aid, over and above $50 million to be transferred from Israel to Jordan.
- Trade Minister Sharansky to play Deep Blue, computer that beat chess champ.
- Passive smoke increases risk of heart disease.
